name: Sotatercept
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 3 weeks; dose titrated by weight with haemoglobin and platelet monitoring

discovery.note: A ligand trap made of the extracellular domain of activin receptor type IIA fused to human IgG1 Fc, first studied for bone loss and anaemia.

tagline: First-in-class activin signalling inhibitor for pulmonary arterial hypertension
summary: Sotatercept is a fusion protein that traps activins and related TGF-β superfamily ligands. Approved in 2024, it is the first PAH therapy designed to target the vascular remodelling underlying the disease rather than only dilating vessels.
mechanism: In PAH, signalling via the BMPR2 pathway, which restrains proliferation, is reduced, while pro-proliferative activin/GDF signalling through ActRIIA–SMAD2/3 is increased.

Sotatercept binds activin A, GDF8, GDF11 and other ligands, rebalancing these pathways. In models and patients this reduces pulmonary vascular wall thickening and lowers pulmonary vascular resistance.
uses: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO group I) in adults, added to background therapy

history.title: Merck acquires Acceleron
history.detail: Merck completes its acquisition of Acceleron, gaining sotatercept.

history.title: STELLAR trial
history.detail: Phase 3 STELLAR (NEJM) shows improved 6-minute walk distance and fewer clinical worsening events.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: European Commission approves Winrevair in August.

history.title: Outcome trials
history.detail: ZENITH results in high-risk PAH (stopped early for efficacy) show fewer deaths, lung transplants or PAH hospitalisations.

pk.metabolism: Catabolism to peptides and amino acids

facts: Sotatercept was originally developed as a treatment for anaemia and bone loss before its effect on pulmonary vessels was explored.
Luspatercept, a related ActRIIB-Fc ligand trap, is used for anaemia.
